title: Lecture 3 Part 1 — Applications
description: Apply CSS rules, selectors, colors, and text properties to common web page styling scenarios.
subject: Web Development

questions.question: You want to make a single `<h2>` heading red using an inline style. Which code is correct?
questions.explanation: The style attribute applies a CSS declaration directly to this h2 element, and color sets its text color.

questions.question: You are configuring an embedded style sheet to change the background of the entire page to gray. Where should this code be placed?
options: At the very bottom of the `<body>` section.
In the `<head>` section of the HTML document.
As an attribute inside the `<html>` tag.
questions.correctAnswer: In the `<head>` section of the HTML document.
questions.explanation: Embedded stylesheet rules belong inside <style> in the document head, where they can style the page.

questions.question: You have an external style sheet named `styles.css`. What is the correct way to link it to your HTML document?
questions.explanation: Use <link> with rel="stylesheet" and href to associate the external CSS file with the document.

questions.question: You have a `p` element. An external style sheet sets its color to blue. An embedded style sets its color to green. An inline style sets its color to red. What color will the text be?
questions.explanation: For the declarations described, the inline style has higher precedence than the external and embedded rules, so red is used.

questions.question: You created a CSS class named "highlight" (`.highlight { background-color: yellow; }`). How do you apply this to a paragraph?
questions.explanation: The class attribute connects the paragraph to the .highlight selector.

questions.question: You want a unique navigation bar to have a black background. You create the CSS rule `#navbar { background-color: black; }`. How do you apply this to a `<div>`?
questions.explanation: The id attribute connects this div to the #navbar selector.

questions.question: You want to style only the `<a>` (hyperlink) tags that are inside a `<footer>` element. Which descendant selector should you use?
questions.explanation: A space between footer and a selects descendant links anywhere inside a footer.

questions.question: You want to configure your text to be italicized. Which property and value pair should you use?
questions.explanation: font-style controls italic styling; font-weight controls boldness instead.

questions.question: You notice that a hyperlink is underlined, and you want to remove the underline. Which CSS rule achieves this?
questions.explanation: The text-decoration property controls link underlining, and none removes that decoration.

questions.question: You want to make a paragraph's text completely capitalized. Which CSS property handles this?
questions.explanation: The text-transform property changes letter case for display; uppercase makes the text capitalized.

questions.question: You want to center the text inside an `<h1>` element. Which CSS declaration should you use?
questions.explanation: The text-align property aligns the inline content within the heading; center centers it.

questions.question: You want to apply a drop shadow to your text. The CSS property is `text-shadow`. According to the lecture, what do the first two numerical values represent in `text-shadow: 2px 4px 5px red;`?
questions.explanation: text-shadow values begin with horizontal offset and vertical offset, followed by blur radius and color.

questions.question: You are defining a `font-family`. Which of the following is the best practice according to web standards?
questions.explanation: Providing fallback typefaces lets the browser use another available font; the generic sans-serif family is a robust final fallback.

questions.question: You want to indent the first line of a paragraph. Which CSS property should you use?
questions.explanation: text-indent sets the indentation of the first formatted line in a block of text.

questions.question: A client asks you to center the entire webpage layout on the screen. Which CSS technique is commonly used on a container `<div>` to achieve this?
questions.explanation: Auto horizontal margins distribute the available side space evenly around a fixed-width or max-width block, centering it.

questions.question: You want to make the text inside a `<strong>` tag extra bold (bolder than normal). Which property do you modify?
questions.explanation: font-weight sets text boldness; strong already carries semantic importance, while CSS controls its visual weight.

questions.question: You want to apply the same CSS rules to both `<h1>` and `<h2>` tags without writing the rules twice. How do you format the selector?
questions.explanation: Comma-separated selectors apply the same rule set independently to both h1 and h2 elements.

questions.question: You want to use a web-safe hexadecimal color shorthand for red. Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: #F00 is the three-digit shorthand for #FF0000 because each hex digit is repeated.

questions.question: You need to change the color of a single word inside a paragraph to green without breaking the paragraph to a new line. Which HTML tag combined with CSS is best for this?
questions.explanation: <span> stays inline within the paragraph, making it suitable for styling one word without introducing a line break.

questions.question: You are using the HSL color notation in CSS3: `hsl(0, 100%, 50%)`. What do the three values represent respectively?
questions.explanation: HSL stands for hue, saturation, and lightness, in that order.
